chose: Low priority through exec wrappers resolved on PATH: nice -n 10, plus taskpolicy -c utility on macOS, applied only when the program itself resolves. lowPriority and verifySlot are DriveOptions that the CLI always sets, as it sets keepAwake
over: os.setPriority on the child after spawn; taskpolicy -b (darwin background); defaulting both on in the library
because: setPriority races a shell's first fork. -b confines the process to the efficiency cores and throttles its I/O, which would slow every driven test run. An unresolved binary spawned through a wrapper would exit 127 (nice) or 66 (taskpolicy) instead of failing with ENOENT and spawn_error. Library callers include parallel vitest workers that share one hermetic state base, and a default-on slot would serialize their verifications.
